subject: history_social
passage: When Leonardo of Pisa, now known as Fibonacci, completed his Liber Abaci in 1202, most European merchants still kept their accounts in Roman numerals. Drawing on methods he had learned as a young man in North Africa, Leonardo showed readers how the nine "Indian figures" and the sign for zero could simplify the arithmetic of trade: converting between currencies, which varied from city to city; dividing profits among partners, often in unequal ______ converting weights and measures, a chore complicated by the many local standards then in use.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: After the colon, the text lists three tasks, and each one contains its own comma ("currencies, which varied …"; "partners, often in unequal shares"; "measures, a chore …"). When items in a series contain internal commas, semicolons must separate the items. The first two items are already separated by a semicolon, so a semicolon must also come before "and" and the final item.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A colon can't separate items in a series, and the sentence already uses a colon to introduce the list.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Because the items in this series contain their own commas, a comma can't separate them; the series already uses a semicolon, and the separators must be consistent.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without a separating mark, the second and third items in the series run together.
explanation.D: Correct. The semicolon separates the last two items in a series whose items contain internal commas, matching the semicolon used earlier in the list.
